# CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - Google Chrome Security

Locks down Google Chrome security to the same level as Edge: Safe Browsing on and impossible to bypass, malicious downloads blocked, certificate errors cannot be clicked through, and no company data to a personal Google account.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Google Chrome policy in the settings catalog (chromeintunev1, chromeintunev141) — values chosen to match the Edge counterpart in this baseline; ids, options and ranges verified against DCv2/Settings in pl4nty/intune-change-tracking |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Google_Chrome_Security.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Google_Chrome_Security.json) |

> Safe Browsing on standard (1), not enhanced (2): enhanced sends every visited URL to Google. Download restriction 4 is 'block malicious downloads', the same value as in Edge. The password manager is turned off because Edge is the managed password manager; Chrome no longer saves new passwords, while passwords already saved keep working according to Google. Extensions have their own policy (Google Chrome Extensions), as with Edge; BlockExternalExtensions is here, because it only affects extensions that other software installs through the registry. ApplicationBoundEncryptionEnabled lives in the chromeintunev141 namespace in the catalog, the rest in chromeintunev1. Firefox has no settings catalog definitions: see extras/windows/remediations/firefox-policies.
